Manufacturers: same as applicant (Applicant & Manufacturer). I'll include the same.

Certified type:
- Category: This is "electronic calculating and indicating device" for dynamic measuring systems for liquids other than water. Category could be "Indicator" or "Electronic calculating and indicating device". Given the schema examples ("Load cell", "Indicator", "Measuring system", "Fuel dispenser", "Taximeter", "Gas meter", ...), I'd use "Electronic calculating and indicating device" as it's the stated identification. Actually for R117-1, calculating and indicating device... Let me use "Indicator" or the exact description. I'll use "Electronic calculating and indicating device".
- Type designations: LCR.iQ, LCRx.iQ, Masterload.iQ, Masterloadx.iQ
- Module designation: null (not applicable, since this is a calculating and indicating device, not a load cell). Actually the schema says module_designation: "Analog load cell" | "Not applicable" | null. This isn't a load cell certificate; I'd say null or omit. I'll use "Not applicable"? Hmm — better to omit since it's not mentioned. Actually rule 8 says don't fabricate. I'll omit it or set to null. I'll set null.
- Description: "An electronic calculating and indicating device" — "Intended for the measurement of: Liquids other than water"

Model family: 4 model variants: LCR.iQ, LCRx.iQ, Masterload.iQ, Masterloadx.iQ. These are type designations rather than model variants of a family... The cert covers 4 types. The model_family should be included only if cert covers >1 model variant. Yes, 4 types. I'll include model_family with models as the 4 type designations. family_name: null.

Components: The software parts? The table lists software: LCR.iQ software (SR1000), I/O board software (SR1010), SENSEiQ board software (SR1011). These are software components. Could record as components with role "software". The schema says components[] for sub-assemblies. The software identification table lists software parts: GNU/Linux 4.9.88-007, LCR.iQ software parts SR1000 v1.07...v1.12.00, I/O board software SR1010 v1.06...v1.12.00, SENSEiQ board software SR1011 v1.00.01...v1.12.00. These are alternatives (OR) within each board's software versions. I could record as components:
- role: "GNU/Linux operating system", type_designations: ["4.9.88-007"], characteristics: checksum...
- role: "LCR.iQ software part", type_designations: ["SR1000"], versions...
- role: "I/O board software part", type_designations: ["SR1010"], ...
- role: "SENSEiQ board software part", type_designations: ["SR1011"], ...

This seems reasonable. But maybe simpler: record software identification in characteristics type_level or a matrix table. The schema says components[] include ONLY if cert names sub-assemblies. The software parts are named sub-assemblies (I/O board, SENSEiQ board). I'll include components with alternatives "OR" for version alternatives.

Hmm, but components' characteristics are objects. Let me structure:

components[]:
- {role: "Operating system", type_designations: ["GNU/Linux 4.9.88-007"], alternatives: null, characteristics: {checksum: "060afc2bc6f029379c15ece991aa6eb8"}}
- {role: "LCR.iQ software part", type_designations: ["SR1000"], alternatives: "OR", characteristics: {versions: [{version: "v1.07", checksum: "..."}...]}}

Hmm, but "alternatives" is about alternatives between type_designations, not versions. Maybe better to list each software version as a type_designation: ["SR1000 v1.07", "SR1000 v1.08.01", ...]. That preserves alternatives "OR" among them. And characteristics: checksums as a mapping? That's messy.

Alternatively use matrix_tables for the software table. That fits well: matrix_tables with name "Software identification", columns [part, description, version, checksum], rows for each. That preserves everything. Then also model_family? No — software versions aren't model variants.

I think best: components for the three software parts (LCR.iQ software, I/O board software, SENSEiQ board software) with type_designations listing all versions, and a matrix_table preserving the full software identification table including checksums.

Actually, let me reconsider. The schema says components[] include ONLY if cert names sub-assemblies. The cert names: "LCR.iQ software part", "I/O board software part", "SENSEiQ board software part". These are software parts, arguably sub-assemblies. I'll include them as components with characteristics including version-checksum pairs.

Let me do:

components: [
  {
    "role": "Operating system",
    "type_designations": ["GNU/Linux 4.9.88-007"],
    "alternatives": null,
    "characteristics": {"checksum": "060afc2bc6f029379c15ece991aa6eb8"}
  },
  {
    "role": "LCR.iQ software part",
    "type_designations": ["SR1000 v1.07", "SR1000 v1.08.01", "SR1000 v1.09.01", "SR1000 v1.09.03", "SR1000 v1.11.00", "SR1000 v1.12.00"],
    "alternatives": "OR",

      "checksums": {
        "SR1000 v1.07": "b22c8503bfe9924042aa7002cf5777b4",
        ...
      }
    }
  },
  ...
]

That works.

Also a matrix_table for the software identification. Actually maybe that's redundant. But schema says preserve multi-dim tables that don't fit elsewhere. The software table has columns DESCRIPTION/VERSION/CHECKSUM grouped by part. I'll include a matrix_table "Software identification" with columns [software_part, description, version, checksum] and rows.

- ambient_temperature_range: {min: -40, max: 70}, unit "°C", note "condensing humidity" — could add footnote or separate note. I'll add value {min:-40, max:70}, unit_symbol "°C". Maybe include a note in characteristics? There's no note field. I could put "condensing_humidity": true as separate type_level characteristic.

- documentation_folder_number: "TC11730-2"? That's in text: "The construction of the measuring instrument is recorded in the Documentation folder no. TC11730-2." Could include as documentation_file in test_reports? The test_reports role includes documentation_file. The documentation folder no. TC11730-2 — record as test_report entry with role "documentation_file", id "TC11730-2", no date. Rule 8: don't fabricate. Date omitted.
